title: NBA Offseason Daily Digest
subtitle: July 29, 2026 – Free Agency Heats Up, LeBron Joins Sixers!

items.headline: LeBron James Officially Signs with Philadelphia 76ers!
items.summary: The King has a new home! LeBron James has officially signed a two-year deal with the Philadelphia 76ers for the veteran's minimum of $8 million. James announced his decision on social media, calling it his 'last decision' after considering retirement. He joins a formidable roster featuring Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, and recent acquisition Jaylen Brown, instantly making the Sixers championship contenders.

items.headline: Nuggets Face Potential Nikola Jokic Trade Scenario Amidst Financial Squeeze
items.summary: The Denver Nuggets are reportedly grappling with the harsh realities of the NBA's second apron, leading to concerns about the future of three-time MVP Nikola Jokic. After matching the OKC Thunder's offer sheet for Spencer Jones, Denver officially entered the second apron, prompting owner Josh Kroenke to acknowledge scenarios he 'never wants to contemplate' regarding their star player.

items.headline: Warriors Passed on Blockbuster Jaylen Brown Trade, ESPN Reports
items.summary: According to ESPN's Shams Charania, the Golden State Warriors opted against trading for All-NBA forward Jaylen Brown at last season's trade deadline. The Boston Celtics reportedly demanded four first-round picks, a price the Warriors were unwilling to meet, a decision that could have significant implications for their future title contention around Stephen Curry.

items.headline: DeMar DeRozan Reportedly Willing to Sign Veteran Minimum for Championship Pursuit
items.summary: Veteran six-time All-Star DeMar DeRozan is reportedly open to signing for the veteran's minimum in his quest for an NBA championship, as free agency continues to heat up. This development could make him a highly sought-after role player for contending teams.

items.headline: Mario Hezonja Inks One-Year Deal with Cavaliers
items.summary: Former No. 5 overall pick Mario Hezonja has signed a one-year, $2.8 million contract with the Cleveland Cavaliers. After five NBA seasons, Hezonja spent time overseas before returning to the league.

items.headline: OKC Thunder Match Spencer Jones Offer Sheet
items.summary: The Oklahoma City Thunder have successfully matched a two-year, $12 million offer sheet for emerging forward Spencer Jones. This move retains the restricted free agent with the Thunder, preventing him from joining another team.

items.headline: Chicago Bulls Reportedly Pursuing Clippers RFA Bennedict Mathurin
items.summary: The Chicago Bulls have emerged as a potential suitor for Los Angeles Clippers restricted free agent Bennedict Mathurin. According to Marc Stein, the Bulls are showing interest, joining the Pelicans in the pursuit of the young talent.

items.headline: Nuggets Bolster Coaching Staff with Dave Joerger as Lead Assistant
items.summary: The Denver Nuggets are adding veteran coaching experience to their bench, hiring Dave Joerger as the team's lead assistant coach under David Adelman. Joerger brings extensive head coaching experience from his stints with the Memphis Grizzlies and Sacramento Kings.

items.headline: Houston Rockets Bring in Chip Engelland as Assistant Coach
items.summary: The Houston Rockets have reportedly hired renowned shooting and development coach Chip Engelland as an assistant on Ime Udoka's staff. Engelland's expertise is expected to significantly aid the development and shooting growth of Rockets players, including rising star Amen Thompson.

items.headline: Paris Basketball Finalizing Deal with Former NBA Forward Alize Johnson
items.summary: Paris Basketball is reportedly close to finalizing a deal to sign former NBA forward Alize Johnson for the 2026-27 season. The 30-year-old brings five seasons of NBA experience with several teams to the European club.

items.headline: Early Odds: OKC and Spurs Lead 2027 Championship Favorites
items.summary: Despite LeBron James joining the Philadelphia 76ers, oddsmakers still view the Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs as the leading favorites for the 2027 NBA title. The Thunder are led by two-time MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, while the Spurs boast Defensive Player of the Year Victor Wembanyama.
